name: Crush

surfaces.label: crush in a terminal (default command; also `crush -s <id>` and `crush -C`). One native Go binary named `crush`. By default the agent runs inside this same process. npm installs the same binary at node_modules/@charmland/crush/bin/crush (downloaded by the postinstall script, and again by run-crush.js if missing) and launches it as a child of `node run-crush.js` (that node parent does not match; the crush child does). With CRUSH_CLIENT_SERVER=1 this process is a client and the agent (LLM stream, tools, database writes) runs in the separate `crush server` daemon below, so the client has no tool children and the turn's db writes come from the daemon; whether the client's own cpu stays low is not verified.

crush server: detached background server (Setsid) that the client auto-starts only when CRUSH_CLIENT_SERVER=1 is set (opt-in in v0.97.0); `crush server` can also be run by hand. Its parent is the client that spawned it until that client exits, then launchd, so the probe's outermost-process rule hides it while that client is alive. It shuts itself down 60 s after its last workspace is released. Listens on unix socket $TMPDIR/crush-<uid>.sock (or $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, or /tmp/crush-<uid>.sock when the path exceeds 104 bytes). Loose match: args_contain is a substring test, so exclude_args carries every other subcommand (a `crush run "restart the server"` line would otherwise match).

working_signals.name: <project>/.crush/crush.db-wal
working_signals.meaning: Every streamed text and reasoning delta is written to the messages table (SQLite, WAL mode), coalesced to one write per ~33 ms. The db is per project, found by walking up from the process cwd to the nearest .crush directory (or --data-dir), and shared by every crush process in that project, so a fresh -wal mtime says 'some session in this project wrote to the db', not which one or that a turn is running (other writes, such as file tracking, also touch it). Quiet during a long tool run or a slow first token, so 15 s is an unmeasured guess. No per_session path is given because the file is not per session.

Unmeasured floor. Source: the chat redraws a spinner animation at 20 fps (internal/ui/anim/anim.go fps = 20, driven from internal/ui/model/chat.go) while items are pending, and the UI has no idle ticker of comparable rate. Not observed on a live instance.

waiting_signals.meaning: On macOS a local session sends an OSC 99 or OSC 777 terminal notification titled 'Crush is waiting...' with message 'Permission required to execute "<tool>"' or 'N questions need your input'. The same title is used when the turn finishes ('Agent's turn completed in ...'), so tell them apart by the message. Sent only when the terminal reports focus events and the Crush window is NOT focused, and notifications is not 'disabled'. Terminal-side only, no file or process trace. notifications option: auto, native, osc, bell, disabled.
Inside a herdr pane (HERDR_ENV=1) crush reports state idle, working or blocked over HERDR_SOCKET_PATH with pane.report_agent. blocked means a permission request is pending. Only readable by herdr.

Client-server mode only: GET /v1/workspaces/{id}/events on the unix socket streams permission and question requests, and GET /v1/workspaces/{id}/agent returns is_busy. Not reachable in the default single-process mode.

hooks.config: hooks object in ~/.config/crush/crush.json, project crush.json or .crush.json, or `hook add` in crushrc (~/.config/crush/crushrc, ./crushrc, ./.crushrc). Project overrides global.

telemetry.how: No OpenTelemetry exporter in the source. Only PostHog product metrics to https://data.charm.land, disabled by CRUSH_DISABLE_METRICS=1, DO_NOT_TRACK=1 or options.disable_metrics. go.mod lists otel only as indirect dependencies.

notes: Not installed on the research Mac, so no surface was classified live. Sessions sharing a project share one crush.db, so a process maps to a project by cwd, and to one session only when started with -s. `crush run` (non-interactive) is deliberately not a surface: it is excluded from every match and, while alive, is by definition mid-turn. Windows names and paths are out of scope. Homebrew formula path (/opt/homebrew/Cellar/crush/...) is inferred from the tap config, not fetched; the match does not depend on it because the executable basename is `crush`. Thresholds are unmeasured heuristics (transcript_write within_seconds 15, tree_cpu floor 3): the source supports the mechanism, not the numbers. The `--session=<id>` form is not read by the probe's session_id_args (space-separated only). A different program that is also named `crush` cannot be told apart by name alone; not checked against other products.
